## Integration recap — round 6 (final)

This round's build failure was a filename collision: `Domain/RestoreIntegrityService.swift` (the deprecated typealias) and `Domain/Persistence/RestoreIntegrityService.swift` (the real implementation) share a basename, and Xcode won't allow that in one target. The fix that emerged through cross-review was correct and important to get right: `GameEngine.swift` (this round's new file) depends directly on the bare `RestoreIntegrityService` name via that typealias, so deleting the typealias file — the first instinct — would have traded one build failure for a worse one. Instead I renamed the *other* file to match its actual type name (`Domain/Persistence/DomainPersistenceRestoreIntegrityService.swift`), leaving the typealias and every caller untouched.

While wiring the actual app root — the thing every round has been waiting on — I found and fixed several more real bugs that only surface when you actually try to assemble the pieces:

- **`GameEngine`'s public initializer couldn't actually be called from outside `Domain/`.** It takes `haptics: HapticsService`, but `HapticsService`/`DefaultHapticsService` were both `internal`. Swift doesn't allow a public API to expose an internal type in its signature — this would have been an immediate compile error the moment anything tried to construct a real `GameEngine`. Made both public.
- **The `SettingsView` bug Claude A flagged herself:** draw-mode changes were writing straight to `SettingsStore`, bypassing `GameEngine.setDrawMode(_:)` — which is the only place that safely finalizes the active session and redeals in the new mode. That would have silently desynced a running game from its own settings file. Rewired `SettingsViewModel` to a sync-only pattern (`syncDrawMode`/`syncTimerEnabled`) and `SettingsView` to route both draw-mode and timer changes through `GameEngine`, with `hasActiveGame` now reading `engine.state.terminalState == .active` instead of a hardcoded `true`.
